record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Parallel machines with additive common time function
record.original_question: Given n jobs to be scheduled on m identical parallel machines, where job j has time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = a_j + f(t) when it starts at time t, with a_j job-specific and f a common function of starting time, determine the computational complexity of minimizing the makespan C_max. In particular, identify assumptions on f(t), beyond the already known necessary optimality condition, that yield polynomial-time solvable cases, or prove hardness for the general problem.

evidence.quote: Problem P m|p j=a j+f(t)|C max is open

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following parallel machine scheduling problem with time-dependent processing times. There are n jobs and m identical parallel machines. Each job j (j = 1, ..., n) has an associated nonnegative basic processing time a_j. There is a fixed common function f: [0, ∞) → [0, ∞) such that if job j is started at time t on any machine, its actual processing time equals p_j(t) = a_j + f(t). Each machine processes at most one job at a time, each job is processed on exactly one machine, and preemption is not allowed. The completion time of job j is its starting time plus its processing time. The makespan C_max is the maximum completion time over all jobs.

(a) Determine the computational complexity of minimizing C_max in this model: prove either that the problem is NP-hard in general, or that it admits a polynomial-time algorithm.

(b) Identify natural assumptions on the common function f(t), beyond any necessary conditions for an optimal schedule to exist (such as monotonicity assumptions ensuring a no-idle structural property), under which the problem becomes polynomially solvable, and provide the corresponding algorithms.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of minimizing makespan on m identical parallel machines with processing times of the form p_j(t) = a_j + f(t) is listed as an open problem in surveys on time-dependent scheduling. General scheduling complexity surveys do not report a resolution; the closest related results concern single-machine versions or specific classes of f. No published proof of NP-hardness or polynomial-time algorithm for the general parallel-machine variant was found.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems in machine scheduling complexity; the time-dependent variant Pm|p_j=a_j+f(t)|C_max is not listed as resolved.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the parallel-machine time-dependent makespan problem is reported in recent complexity surveys.

status_evidence.title: An Overview of Some Single Machine Scheduling Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Overview discusses time-dependent scheduling on a single machine; parallel-machine variants with common function f remain unresolved in general.
status_evidence.claim: Single-machine analogues are studied but the parallel-machine general case is not stated as solved.
